items.question: How does the AW169 RFM Section 7 describe the helicopter and its intended roles?
options: Medium twin-engine aircraft designed for land and sea operations including offshore services, HEMS, SAR, law enforcement, corporate and utility roles.
Light single-engine aircraft intended only for inland VFR training operations.
Heavy twin-engine aircraft certified exclusively for offshore oil and gas transport.
Single-engine helicopter optimised only for agricultural spraying and banner towing.
items.explanation: The opening paragraph of Section 7 Helicopter general describes the AW169 as a medium twin-engine aircraft for land and sea operations including offshore services, HEMS, SAR, law enforcement, corporate and utility roles.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Helicopter general (p.7-1)

items.question: According to Helicopter general in Section 7, what does the RFM state about the cockpit seats and flight controls?
options: Pilot and co-pilot have crashworthy seats and double commands (cyclic, collective bar and pedals).
Only the left seat is equipped with flight controls; the right seat is for passengers only.
Both seats are non-crashworthy and share a single set of flight controls.
The cockpit uses side-stick controllers with no conventional pedals.
items.explanation: Section 7 Helicopter general states that the cockpit has pilot and co-pilot crashworthy seats and double commands, including cyclic, collective bar and pedals for both crew members.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Helicopter general (p.7-1)

items.question: How is the main cabin structure described in the AW169 RFM Section 7?
options: Structure forward of the STA8175 joint with metallic internal structures and airframes and composite external fuselage skins, cowlings and fairings.
Entirely composite monocoque shell with no metallic internal structure.
All-metal stressed skin fuselage with no composite components.
Fabric-covered tubular frame with fixed landing gear attachments.
items.explanation: Section 7 states that the main cabin is the structure forward of the STA8175 joint, constructed of metallic internal structures and airframes with composite external fuselage skins, cowlings and fairings.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Helicopter general (p.7-1)

items.question: What is the primary structural feature of the AW169 tail unit according to Section 7?
options: Carbon fibre composite upper and lower longerons providing a continuous load path from the STA8175 joint to the fin.
Steel tube truss bolted directly to the main gearbox.
Aluminium honeycomb tail boom with no longerons.
Fabric-covered fin supported only by the tail rotor gearbox deck.
items.explanation: The Helicopter general text describes the tail unit primary structural parts as carbon fibre composite upper and lower longerons providing a continuous load path from the STA8175 joint to the fin.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Helicopter general (p.7-1)

items.question: Where are the circuit breaker panel and rotor brake control panel located in the AW169 cockpit?
options: In the overhead console above the heads of the flight crew.
On the left side of the main instrument panel.
On the rear cabin bulkhead behind the co-pilot.
Under the floor in the avionics bay.
items.explanation: Section 7 explains that the overhead console, installed above the heads of the flight crew, includes the circuit breaker panel and the rotor brake control panel.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Helicopter general (p.7-1)

items.question: According to Section 7, where are the control panels and displays that govern the installed systems and are used by the flight crew mainly located?
options: On the instrument panel and interseat console between the pilot and co-pilot.
Only on touchscreens in the rear cabin.
On the tail boom and external fuselage.
On the collective sticks exclusively.
items.explanation: The Helicopter general text states that the instrument panel and interseat console contain all the control panels and displays governing the systems installed in the aircraft and utilised by the flight crew.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Helicopter general (p.7-1)

items.question: Which engines and key features does the AW169 RFM list in the Helicopter general section?
options: Two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW210A engines with dual FADEC, APU mode and variable RPM control, installed in the upper deck under cowlings.
Two Rolls-Royce turboshaft engines with manual fuel controls and fixed RPM.
A single PW210A engine with dual FADEC and a fixed-pitch main rotor.
Two piston engines driving separate main rotors without FADEC.
items.explanation: Section 7 describes the power system as two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW210A engines with dual FADEC, APU mode and variable RPM control capability, installed in the upper deck and covered by cowlings.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Helicopter general (p.7-1)

items.question: Where is the flotation control panel for the emergency flotation system installed according to the System Description OES section?
options: On the right side of the interseat console in the cockpit.
In the overhead console above the pilots.
On the left cabin sidewall near the sliding door.
On the aft cabin bulkhead next to the baggage door.
items.explanation: The OES System Description states that the flotation control panel is installed on the right side of the interseat console in the cockpit.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-652)

items.question: How does the crew place the emergency flotation system in the armed condition before flight above water?
options: By setting the FLOAT master switch on the flotation control panel to ARMED.
By pulling the guarded FLOAT switch on the collective grip and leaving it raised.
By selecting AUTO EXT on the landing light switch.
By switching off electrical power to both inflation systems.
items.explanation: Section 7 explains that the emergency flotation system operates only when it is in the armed condition, which is achieved by setting the FLOAT master switch on the flotation control panel to ARMED.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-652)

items.question: What does the RFM describe as the primary means of activating the emergency flotation system when it is armed?
options: Automatic actuation via four emergency float switches (water sensors) when two adjacent switches contact water.
Manual activation only by the pilot using a cable pull handle on the floor.
Automatic deployment whenever airspeed falls below 10 kt at low altitude.
Activation solely by the hoist operator using a panel in the cabin.
items.explanation: The OES System Description states that four emergency float switches on the lower fuselage are connected to the flotation control panel and inflation valves and that this automatic water-sensor activation is considered the primary means of emergency flotation system activation when the master switch is ARMED.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-652 to 7-653)

items.question: When does the RFM require the emergency flotation system to be set to ARMED?
options: When the helicopter is in flight above the water.
Whenever the helicopter is parked on the apron.
Only during maintenance ground runs.
Only after the floats have already been deployed in a ditching.
items.explanation: Section 7 notes that the emergency flotation system must be set in the armed condition when the helicopter is in flight above the water.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-653)

items.question: If the automatic activation of the emergency flotation system fails, how can the crew manually inflate the floats according to Section 7?
options: By raising the guard and pressing the guarded FLOAT pushbutton on either the pilot's or co-pilot's collective grip.
By cycling the FLOAT master switch on the interseat console OFF then ARMED three times.
By selecting STOW on the landing light switch for more than five seconds.
By pulling the rotor brake handle fully aft while on the water.
items.explanation: The OES description explains that, in the event of failure of the automatic actuation method, aircrew can command floats inflation via guarded pushbutton FLOAT switches on both pilot and copilot collective grips.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-653)

items.question: What is the purpose of the TEST button on the flotation control panel as described in the System Description?
options: To check the continuity of the electrical circuits from the control panel to the inflation valves and verify that the system test lights illuminate.
To test the rotor brake operation during ground runs.
To simulate a ditching by partially inflating the floats.
To reset all emergency system cautions in the CAS.
items.explanation: Section 7 states that the TEST button on the flotation control panel is used to verify the correct operation and continuity of the electrical circuits to the inflation valves, with the LH SYS and RH SYS lights illuminating during the test.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Emergency flotation system (p.7-653)

items.question: According to the Lights (Chap 33) system description, how are the steerable landing lights normally controlled and what provides backup control?
options: Primarily by switches on the pilot and co-pilot collective grips, with integrated EDCU external lights page controls acting as backup.
Only by the EDCU external lights page; collective grip switches are backup.
Only by a panel on the overhead console with no backup control.
By a floor-mounted pedal, backed up by the hoist operator's panel.
items.explanation: The Lights chapter states that the external lights are controlled via the EDCU lights page, but that the steerable landing lights are primarily controlled via the related switches on the pilot and co-pilot collective grips, with the integrated EDCU controls acting as backup.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Lights (Chap 33) Steerable landing lights (p.7-302 to 7-305)

items.question: With the AW169 landing lights switched off and in the stowed position, what happens when the AUTO EXT/CAGE position is selected on the AUTO EXT/CAGE STOW switch according to the RFM?
options: The selected landing light(s) illuminate and extend automatically to the predefined landing position, and other controls to the light(s) are inhibited during the sequence.
The selected landing light(s) retract and switch off, completing the STOW function.
The selected landing light(s) flash three times and remain stowed for a lamp test only.
The system switches control of the landing lights from the collective grip to the EDCU page.
items.explanation: The steerable landing lights description explains that with the lights switched off and stowed, selecting AUTO EXT/CAGE initiates the AUTO EXT function: the selected light(s) illuminate and extend to the predefined landing position and all other controls to the lights are inhibited during the sequence.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Lights (Chap 33) Steerable landing lights (p.7-305 to 7-307)

items.question: On the Hydraulic System (Chap 29) description, what does the interlocking of hydraulic circuits 1 and 2 on the EDCU HYD page ensure when you manage the system from the cockpit?
options: You cannot shut off both hydraulic systems at the same time using the cockpit controls.
Either circuit automatically shuts down whenever you lower collective to idle.
Hydraulic pressures in circuits 1 and 2 are always forced to be identical.
The tail rotor hydraulic circuit is always supplied from system 1 only.
items.explanation: The hydraulic page on the EDCU is described as providing interlocking of the two circuits without the possibility of excluding both systems, so the pilot cannot inadvertently shut off both hydraulic systems at once from the cockpit.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system (Chap 29) Hydraulic system controls and displays (p.7-243)

items.question: According to the Hydraulic System controls and displays description, what happens if one hydraulic circuit has been manually excluded and the remaining circuit later suffers a low-pressure failure?
options: The previously excluded hydraulic circuit is automatically re-activated to restore hydraulic power.
Both hydraulic circuits remain off until the pilot cycles the HYD page and reselects them.
The AFCS disconnects and the helicopter must be landed with no hydraulic assistance.
Only the tail rotor actuator is powered while the main rotor actuators remain depressurised.
items.explanation: The RFM states that the hydraulic system includes automatic re-activation of the excluded circuit in the event of a failure (low pressure) in the other circuit, so that hydraulic power is restored without requiring a cockpit reconfiguration first.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system (Chap 29) Hydraulic system controls and displays (p.7-243)

items.question: What is the primary operational purpose of the Electric Hydraulic Power Supply (EHPS) described in the hydraulic system supplement?
options: To provide just enough hydraulic power on the ground for full and free movement checks of the flight control servo actuators before the engine-driven pumps are used.
To back up the main hydraulic pumps in flight whenever engine NG is below 64%.
To power only the tail rotor actuator during single-engine operations in flight.
To supply emergency pressure to the landing gear actuators during normal gear extension.
items.explanation: The EHPS is described as a 28 VDC electric motor-driven hydraulic power supply installed on hydraulic system 1 that provides hydraulic power just sufficient for the full and free movement check of the servo actuators prior to running the mechanically driven HPSs, and is intended as a ground-use kit.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system (Chap 29) EHPS Supplement (p.S42-1)

items.question: Which limitation applies when you operate the EHPS according to the RFM description?
options: It is for ground use only, powered from the helicopter battery, and its operation is limited to a maximum of 2 minutes at a time.
It may be run continuously in flight as long as both DC generators are online.
It must be switched on for at least 10 minutes before any flight control checks are carried out.
It may only be used in flight above 10 000 ft to prevent pump overheating.
items.explanation: The EHPS description states that the unit is a ground-use component controlled via the HYD page, powered from the helicopter battery and limited by AMMC logic to 2 minutes of operation, which defines how the crew may use it during pre-flight checks.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system (Chap 29) EHPS Supplement (p.S42-1)

items.question: How are the main and tail rotor servo actuators designed to behave if one hydraulic system fails according to the Rotors Flight Control description?
options: They continue to operate on the remaining hydraulic system without degrading the helicopter handling qualities.
They revert to full manual reversion with significantly increased control forces.
They lock in their last position until both hydraulic systems are restored.
The tail rotor actuator remains powered but all main rotor actuators are depressurised.
items.explanation: The Section 7 Rotors Flight Control text explains that both the main rotor and tail rotor servo actuators are designed to operate normally with two completely separated hydraulic systems, and that in case of failure of one system the level of performance with the remaining system ensures no degradation of the helicopter handling qualities.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Rotors flight control (Chap 67) (p.7-562)

items.question: What is the purpose of the Tail Rotor Shut-Off Valve (TRSOV) in the hydraulic system description?
options: To isolate hydraulic circuit 1 from the tail rotor actuator hydraulic line in the event of a leak.
To close both hydraulic systems automatically whenever rotor speed falls below 20% NR.
To cut off hydraulic pressure to the main rotor actuators during rotor brake use only.
To connect hydraulic circuits 1 and 2 together for cross-feed when required.
items.explanation: In the Hydraulic System General description the TRSOV is described as the only component not included in the PCMs, whose function is to enable isolation of hydraulic circuit 1 tail rotor actuator hydraulic line in the event of a leak.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system (Chap 29) General (p.7-241)

items.question: In the Fuel System (Chap 28) general description, which main functions does the airframe fuel system provide for the AW169?
options: Fuel storage, distribution, ventilation and indicating functions supplying both engines in all ground and flight conditions.
Only fuel storage and filtration, with all distribution handled entirely by the engines.
Fuel storage and tyre inflation using bleed air from the engines.
Fuel distribution and de-icing of the main rotor blades through heated fuel.
items.explanation: The Fuel System General paragraph states that the fuel system provides fuel storage capability and supplies the two engines in all ground and flight conditions, and that its principal functions are the fuel storage system, fuel distribution system, fuel ventilation system and fuel indicating system.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) General (p.7-229)

items.question: According to the Fuel System controls and displays description, how can the pilot manually control the fuel shut-off valves (SOVs)?
options: By using the EDCU fuel page to OPEN or CLOSE each fuel SOV.
By pulling guarded fuel levers on the overhead panel above the pilots.
By pressing a pushbutton on each engine control quadrant only.
By selecting crossfeed on the hydraulic page to shut the valves.
items.explanation: The Fuel System controls and displays section explains that the fuel system has both manual and automatic controls and that the manual control is provided on the EDCU fuel page, where the pilot can CLOSE or OPEN the fuel shut-off valves.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) Fuel system controls and displays (p.7-229 to 7-231)

items.question: What does the RFM state happens automatically to the fuel shut-off valve (SOV) in case of an engine fire?
options: The associated fuel SOV closes automatically, which also arms the fire extinguisher for that engine.
Both fuel SOVs open fully to depressurise the fuel lines and prevent vapour lock.
The fuel SOV only partially closes to reduce fuel flow but keep the engine running.
No automatic action occurs; the pilot must always close the fuel SOV manually.
items.explanation: In the description of the fuel system controls and displays the RFM notes that in case of engine fire the relevant fuel shut-off valve is automatically closed, arming the fire extinguisher system for that engine.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) Fuel system controls and displays (p.7-229 to 7-231)

items.question: When a fuel system component malfunctions, which cockpit action does the Fuel System description recommend to obtain more detailed information on the affected component?
options: Display the fuel system synoptic page on the EDCU by selecting the fuel page.
Select the HYD page on the EDCU to check for related cautions.
Switch the FMS to plan view and zoom in on the nearest suitable diversion airfield.
Cycle both engine master switches OFF and ON to reset the indications.
items.explanation: The Fuel System controls and displays paragraph explains that in case of malfunction of a fuel system component it is possible to display the fuel system synoptic page (via the EDCU fuel page) to provide detailed information about the component or components affected by the malfunction.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) Fuel system controls and displays (p.7-229 to 7-231)

items.question: According to the Fuel System description, where are fuel quantities and fuel flow primarily displayed to the crew?
options: On the Multi-Function Display power plant (PWR PLANT) format, in both numerical and graphical form.
Only on a standalone analogue fuel gauge on the overhead panel.
On the AFCS control panel as part of the mode annunciations.
On the CAS window as continuously scrolling text messages.
items.explanation: The text states that fuel quantities and fuel flow are displayed on the Multi-Function Display PWR PLANT format, where they are shown in numerical and graphical representation for the crew.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) Fuel system controls and displays (p.7-230 to 7-231)

items.question: What fuel-related information does the primary flight display (PFD) provide according to the Fuel System cockpit display description?
options: Left, right and total fuel quantities together with the status of both fuel SOVs.
Only total fuel quantity with no indication of individual tank levels.
Separate fuel pressure indications for each engine-driven low pressure pump.
Separate fuel temperature readouts for each main tank and the crossfeed line.
items.explanation: The Fuel System description notes that the primary flight display provides information about left, right and total fuel quantities as well as the status of both fuel shut-off valves, so the pilot can monitor quantities and valve state at a glance.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) Fuel system controls and displays (p.7-231)

items.question: What practical advantage does the Closed Circuit Refuelling Receiver (CCRR) kit provide, and which limitation does the RFM mention for its use?
options: It allows sealed, low-pressure refuelling without fuel fumes or spillage, but cannot be used for gravity refuelling and must be installed together with a gravity filler port.
It enables gravity refuelling only and must not be used with pressure refuelling vehicles under any circumstances.
It allows refuelling in flight with one engine shut down as long as both CCRR units are installed.
It doubles the usable fuel capacity but removes the crash-resistant features of the bladder tanks.
items.explanation: The CCRR kit description states that it allows sealed refuelling without discharge of fuel fumes or fuel spillage to the external environment, but also notes that no gravity refuelling is allowed with this equipment and that it must be installed in conjunction with a gravity filler port.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) LH&RH closed circuit refuelling receiver kit (p.7-239)

items.question: What is the main purpose of the fuel tank ventilation system as described in the Fuel System ventilation section?
options: To ensure proper ventilation of all tanks, prevent adverse pressure across the tank walls and minimise fuel spillage, including during unusual attitudes or rollover, by routing vents to a single underside outlet.
To supply bleed air to de-ice the rotor blades and windshield using fuel vapour.
To cool the fuel before it reaches the engines in high ambient temperatures by venting it through the fuselage roof.
To pressurise the tanks so that boost pumps are not required for engine fuel supply.
items.explanation: The ventilation system description states that the fuel tank ventilation system ensures proper ventilation of all tanks and minimises fuel leakage due to a helicopter rollover by routing vent lines through the fuselage roof to a single underside outlet, preventing adverse pressure conditions across the tank walls while venting fuel vapour overboard.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) Ventilation system (p.7-235)

items.question: Why does the Fuel System description state that flexible pipes are used in certain parts of the fuel lines and that all pipes and hoses are labelled for flow direction and function?
options: To meet crash safety requirements by allowing movement between the bladder tanks and rigid structure without tearing the tanks, and to make the routing and troubleshooting of fuel lines clear to maintenance and flight crews.
To reduce fuel weight by using thinner walls than rigid pipes, even if this increases the risk of leaks.
To allow pilots to manually reroute fuel in flight by twisting the hoses into different positions.
To enable the fuel tanks to be used as an emergency oxygen source when required.
items.explanation: The Fuel System description explains that flexible pipes are used where relative movement between bladder and rigid pipe in a survivable crash could otherwise damage the bladders and cause serious fuel spillage, and that all pipes and hoses are labelled to indicate flow direction and function, enhancing crash safety and system clarity.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system (Chap 28) Fuel distribution system (p.7-232)

items.question: What does the AFCS System Description state happens when you press the TEST push-button on the AFCS control panel before flight?
options: A Pre-Flight Test (PFT) sequence is started, the TEST button remains illuminated during the test, and extinguishes when the test is complete with results shown on the AFCS synoptic page.
The autopilot immediately disconnects all upper modes and switches to basic ATT mode until engine start is complete.
The AFCS resets all mode references and clears any CAS messages related to AFCS without further indication.
The AFCS forces engagement of both AP1 and AP2 channels and automatically selects ALT and HDG modes.
items.explanation: The AFCS controls and displays section in Chapter 22 explains that pressing the TEST push-button on the AFCS control panel initiates a Pre-Flight Test (PFT). The button is illuminated during the test and extinguishes upon completion, with test results indicated on the AFCS page.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS control panel (p.7-31)

items.question: According to the AFCS controls and displays description, what is the effect of pressing the ATT push-button on the AFCS control panel?
options: It engages both AFCS autopilot channels and/or disengages all upper modes and engages ATT mode, depending on avionic phase, providing basic attitude hold.
It disconnects both autopilot channels and leaves all upper modes active in the background.
It arms all available AFCS upper modes without engaging any mode until a separate AP button is pressed.
It directly commands a go-around with automatic transition-up and climb to a pre-set altitude.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description notes that pressing the ATT push-button either engages both autopilot channels 1 and 2 (for Avionic Phase 6.0 and later) or disengages all AFCS upper modes and engages ATT mode, giving basic attitude hold. In both cases it is the primary control to establish ATT mode.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS control panel (p.7-32)

items.question: How does the AP OFF push-button on the cyclic grip affect the AFCS, according to the AFCS System Description?
options: A double press within two seconds disengages both autopilot channels and terminates all AFCS modes and functions, while a single press arms AP OFF without immediate effect until pressed again.
A single press always re-engages all AFCS upper modes that were last active before AP OFF was used.
It only disconnects the yaw channel while leaving pitch and roll autopilot channels engaged.
It switches AFCS from coupled to uncoupled operation while keeping all modes active.
items.explanation: The AFCS controls and displays text explains that for Avionic Phase 8.0 or later a double press of the AP OFF push-button within two seconds causes disengagement of both autopilot channels AP1 and AP2 and termination of all AFCS modes and functions. The first press arms AP OFF, indicated by an advisory on the PFD.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS control panel and cyclic grip controls (p.7-32)

items.question: What effect does engaging the WLVL (Wing Level) mode via its push-button have on AFCS operation?
options: It engages fixed pitch and roll attitude references, has high priority, and causes disengagement of all other AFCS modes.
It only trims out lateral cyclic forces without affecting any engaged AFCS modes.
It adjusts the heading reference bug to the current track but leaves other modes unchanged.
It forces the helicopter into a coordinated turn at the last selected bank angle.
items.explanation: The AFCS description states that once WLVL is engaged the AFCS acquires fixed pitch and roll attitude references. WLVL mode is described as having high priority and causing disengagement of all other AFCS modes.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS control panel (p.7-32)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what is the operational effect of pressing the GA/TU push-button on the cyclic grip in approach or low-altitude operations?
options: It engages Go-Around and/or Transition-Up modes as applicable, has high priority, and causes disengagement of all other AFCS modes so that the AFCS commands the go-around/transition-up profile.
It simply increases the IAS reference by 10 kt while keeping all other modes engaged.
It arms, but does not engage, the go-around mode until collective is raised above a defined detent.
It disconnects the autopilot completely and leaves the pilot flying manually with no AFCS assistance.
items.explanation: The AFCS controls and displays section explains that pressing the GA/TU push-button causes engagement of one or more modes (GA and, for certain avionic phases, TU). GA/TU mode has high priority and causes disengagement of all AFCS modes, giving the AFCS authority to fly the go-around or transition-up profile.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS control panel and cyclic grip controls (p.7-32)

items.question: How is the P/R permanent force trim for the cyclic engaged and indicated according to the AFCS System Description?
options: By using the P/R PTR function on the AFCS page of the EDCU, which when engaged shows a green label and, if disengaged, removes the label and generates a P/R TRIM OFF advisory and ATT OFF caution on CAS.
By pulling a guarded TRIM circuit breaker, which illuminates a P/R TRIM ON caption on the AFCS synoptic page.
By pressing the WLVL push-button on the AFCS control panel, which automatically sets the P/R trim and shows a white WLVL label.
By rotating the HDG knob fully clockwise, which couples the trim system to the yaw channel only.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description explains that the P/R force trim function is controlled on the AFCS page of the EDCU. When engaged, a green label appears; when disengaged the label disappears and the advisory P/R TRIM OFF and the caution ATT OFF are generated on the CAS.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS synoptic and EDCU AFCS page (p.7-35)

items.question: What is the primary role of the AFCS Low Height protection function as described on the AFCS page?
options: To override AFCS collective mode commands and increase collective as needed to prevent exceeding low height thresholds in hover and cruise.
To automatically disconnect the autopilot whenever radar altimeter height falls below 50 ft AGL.
To reduce engine power and increase airspeed whenever height is below 200 ft AGL.
To hold current radar altitude exactly and inhibit any manual collective input below a set limit.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description states that the LOW HT indication on the AFCS page shows that the Low Height protection system is active, overriding AFCS collective mode control to avoid exceeding the defined low height thresholds by automatically increasing collective if they are approached.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS synoptic page (p.7-35)

items.question: According to the AFCS description, what does the PWR LIM indication on the AFCS synoptic page tell the crew?
options: That the AFCS Power Limit/Autorotation protection system is overriding collective mode commands to keep power margin or prevent entry into autorotation.
That engine torque has fallen below idle and the rotor is in full autorotation.
That both generators are offline and the AFCS is powered from the battery only.
That the autopilot channels are inoperative and only manual SAS is available.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description explains that the PWR LIM indication on the AFCS page means the AFCS Power Limit/Autorotation protection system is active, overriding collective mode commands either to maintain power margin or to prevent entry into autorotation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS synoptic page (p.7-35)

items.question: What does the AFCS System Description state happens to AFCS collective modes when the UCPL indication appears on the AFCS page after transition to OEI and power above continuous OEI (COEI)?
options: AFCS collective mode is automatically uncoupled, and will recouple automatically when power is reduced below COEI and the pilot releases the collective.
AFCS collective mode is locked at its last command and can only be changed by cycling AP1 and AP2 off and on.
All AFCS collective and pitch modes remain engaged but are frozen until both engines are restored to AEO.
The AFCS immediately commands maximum climb power and ignores pilot collective inputs.
items.explanation: The AFCS synoptic description explains that UCPL indicates that the AFCS collective mode has been automatically uncoupled following a transition to OEI with power above continuous OEI. When power is reduced below COEI and the pilot releases the collective, the mode automatically re-couples.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) AFCS synoptic page (p.7-35)

items.question: How does the AFCS System Description explain the role of the SCAS part of the main rotor actuators in assisting the pilot?
options: The AFCS controls the SCAS actuator in series with pilot inputs to adjust main rotor blade pitch in response to attitude changes, with limited authority so that failures or jams do not cause excessive control movements.
The SCAS actuator directly replaces the pilot's cyclic and collective controls in all AFCS modes and removes any need for mechanical linkages.
The SCAS actuator is only used for automatic trimming on the ground and is inactive in flight.
The SCAS actuator is a backup hydraulic pump that maintains system pressure after both engine-driven pumps fail.
items.explanation: The AFCS section describes the main rotor actuators as combining a hydraulic servo actuator and an AFCS electrohydraulic (SCAS) actuator. The AFCS controls the SCAS actuator in response to changes in pitch, roll and yaw, working in series with pilot commands with limited authority so that even if it fails or jams, flight control movement and resulting disturbance are limited.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22) Main Rotor Actuators and SCAS (p.7-36)

items.question: In the Electrical Power System description, what is the stated main purpose of the electrical system on the AW169?
options: To provide electrical power to helicopter systems and to start the engines.
To supply backup hydraulic pressure to the primary servos in flight.
To drive the main rotor in case of dual engine failure.
To maintain cabin pressurisation at all operating altitudes.
items.explanation: The opening paragraph of the Electrical Power (Chapter 24) System Description states that the main purpose of the electrical system is to provide electrical power to the helicopter systems and to start the engines.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power (Chap 24) General (p.7-119)

items.question: According to the Electrical Power controls and displays description, what is the role of the EDCU electrical page for the crew?
options: It provides an integrated synoptic of the DC electrical generation and distribution system and allows the crew to control breakers, generator switches and bus tie logic.
It only displays total battery voltage and frequency without any control capability.
It is used exclusively to schedule load shedding in flight by entering numerical load priorities.
It acts as a backup primary flight display when the main PFD fails.
items.explanation: The Electrical Power controls and displays section explains that the EDCU electrical page is the main interface for the crew to monitor and control the DC generation and distribution system, including generator and bus tie status and selected circuit breakers, presented in synoptic form.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power (Chap 24) Electrical power controls and displays (p.7-120)

items.question: What does the description of the 75A Electrical Power Socket kit say about how and when that socket is powered?
options: It is a 28 VDC socket supplied via Non Essential Bus #2 that is automatically powered at helicopter power-up without requiring any dedicated switch.
It is a 115 VAC socket that must be manually switched on using a dedicated breaker before each use.
It is powered only when both main generators are online and is automatically disconnected on the ground.
It is an external AC socket that can only be used during engine start with external power connected.
items.explanation: The System Description for the Kit Electrical power socket (75A) states that it is a 28 VDC connector providing 75 A and is supplied via Non Essential Bus #2, and that it is automatically supplied at helicopter power-up with no requirement to switch the kit on separately.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power (Chap 24) Kit Electrical power socket (75A) (p.7-150)

items.question: According to the External Hoist kit System Description, what CAS messages help the crew monitor the status of the hoist power and light control?
options: HOIST ON and HOIST LT CTRL ON advisory messages on the MFD, together with RH LDG LT ON when the right landing light is being used as searchlight.
Only a single HOIST FAIL warning message without any separate indication of light control.
A generic OES ON advisory whenever any OES kit, including floats and hoist, is powered.
A CARGO HOOK ON caption whenever the hoist is powered to avoid confusion.
items.explanation: The External Hoist kit description states that when the hoist system is selected ON a HOIST ON advisory is generated, and that HOIST LT CTRL ON indicates that the right steerable landing light is being used as searchlight via the hoist light control. RH LDG LT ON is also shown when the right landing light is illuminated, so the crew can correlate these advisories during hoist operations.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES External hoist kit (p.7-709 to 7-712)

items.question: In the Cargo Hook System Description, what is the purpose of the hook cameras kit for the operating crew?
options: To provide a fixed video view of the cargo hook and load on the MFD video page so the crew can visually monitor the hook and payload during external load operations.
To automatically analyse load swing and command AFCS damping without pilot input.
To provide NVG-compatible landing guidance pictures for night approaches.
To record high-definition mission footage for later debriefing only.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook Cameras kit description explains that its purpose is to allow the crew to monitor the cargo hook system and the load fixed at the end of the cable, by providing NTSC video that can be displayed on the MFD video page when the camera is enabled via the EDCU.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook cameras kit (p.7-723)

items.question: According to the External Hoist kit description, what is the correct way to arm the HOIST CUT system before starting hoist operations?
options: Select HOIST ON, confirm the HOIST ON CAS message, then set the HOIST CUT switch to ARM and check that the HOIST CUT ARM CAS message appears.
Set the HOIST CUT switch to ARM before powering the hoist so the cutter cartridge is already energised when HOIST ON is selected.
Pull the HOIST CUT circuit breaker and then push it in again to arm the cutter before extending the cable.
Press and hold the pilot hoist control switch fully down for more than 3 seconds to arm the cutter.
items.explanation: The External Hoist kit System Description states that, after selecting the hoist system ON and confirming the HOIST ON indication, the HOIST CUT switch must be set to ARM so that a HOIST CUT ARM CAS message appears, indicating that the cable cutter system is armed for foul protection.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES External hoist kit, HOIST CUT system (p.7-711)

items.question: What does the System Description say triggers the HOIST CBL FOUL indication and cable cut when the HOIST CUT system is ARMED?
options: A cable angular displacement beyond the preset limits, indicating that the cable is fouled or snagged.
Any momentary loss of electrical power to the hoist drum motor during a lift.
Operation of the pilot hoist control switch to the UP detent for longer than 10 seconds.
Selection of the RH landing light as searchlight while the cable is extended.
items.explanation: The HOIST CUT description explains that, with the system armed, an excessive cable angular displacement beyond preset limits will generate a HOIST CBL FOUL indication and command the cable cutter to operate, protecting the helicopter from a fouled hoist cable.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES External hoist kit, HOIST CUT system (p.7-711)

items.question: In the External Hoist kit description, how is the right steerable landing light used during hoist operations when HOIST LT CTRL is selected?
options: It is controlled through the hoist control pendant as a searchlight, and a HOIST LT CTRL ON CAS message indicates that the hoist has taken control of the right landing light.
It remains under the standard landing light switch on the overhead panel, and HOIST LT CTRL only changes the light colour.
It automatically sweeps the ground ahead of the helicopter without any crew control when HOIST LT CTRL is selected.
It is switched off whenever HOIST LT CTRL is active to avoid glare for the cabin crew.
items.explanation: The External Hoist kit System Description explains that when HOIST LT CTRL is selected, the right steerable landing light is controlled by the hoist operator through the hoist pendant as a searchlight. A HOIST LT CTRL ON CAS message is displayed to show that the hoist has taken control of the right landing light.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES External hoist kit, lighting control (p.7-710)

items.question: What is the maximum allowable hoist load stated in the External Hoist kit description above 0
options: 550 lb (250 kg) above 0, reducing to 500 lb (227 kg) at or below 0.
600 lb (272 kg) at all ambient temperatures.
300 lb (136 kg) above 0 and 250 lb (113 kg) below 0.
550 lb (250 kg) only when the helicopter is in forward flight above 40 KIAS.
items.explanation: The External Hoist kit System Description specifies that the hoist is approved up to 550 lb (approximately 250 kg) for ambient temperatures above 0, and up to 500 lb (approximately 227 kg) at or below 0.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES External hoist kit, limitations (p.7-709)

items.question: According to the External Hoist kit System Description, what lateral bank angle limitation applies with the hoist cable extended?
options: Bank angle must not exceed 20 degrees with the cable extended.
Bank angle must not exceed 10 degrees with the cable extended.
Bank angle is unrestricted provided IAS is below 40 KIAS with the cable extended.
Bank angle is limited to 30 degrees only when the cable is fully reeled in.
items.explanation: The hoist kit description includes an operational limitation stating that when the hoist cable is extended, helicopter bank angle must not exceed 20 degrees.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES External hoist kit, operating limitations (p.7-709)

items.question: How does the Cargo Hook System Description state that the hook is normally opened to release the load in flight?
options: By operating the CARGO REL switch on the cyclic grip, provided the cargo hook system is powered and armed.
By pulling the mechanical release ring on the hook only, since there is no cockpit release.
By selecting HOOK OPEN on the EDCU cargo hook page and waiting for a HOOK OPEN CAS message.
By pressing the EMERG REL pushbutton on the instrument panel during normal release operations.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook System Description describes the normal electrical release as being commanded by the CARGO REL switch on the cyclic grip when the cargo hook system is powered and armed. Mechanical release on the hook and the emergency release function are provided as backups.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook system, controls (p.7-717)

items.question: What is the purpose of the EMERG REL function described in the Cargo Hook System Description?
options: To provide a backup means to open the cargo hook and jettison the external load if the normal CARGO REL control fails.
To lock the hook closed and prevent any release when operating over populated areas.
To automatically release the load at a preset height above ground.
To power the hook cameras kit independently from the rest of the cargo hook system.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook System Description explains that the EMERG REL function provides an emergency means to open the cargo hook and jettison the external load if the normal electrical release via the CARGO REL switch fails, ensuring the helicopter can be freed from the load in abnormal situations.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook system, emergency release (p.7-718)

items.question: According to the Cargo Hook System Description, what do the HOOK ARM and HOOK OPEN CAS messages indicate to the crew?
options: HOOK ARM shows that the cargo hook release system is armed for load release and HOOK OPEN confirms that the hook is actually open.
HOOK ARM indicates that the hook is mechanically locked closed and cannot be opened, while HOOK OPEN means the hook cameras are powered.
HOOK ARM is displayed whenever any OES kit is powered, and HOOK OPEN appears only when the floats are inflated.
HOOK ARM means the hook electrical power is off, and HOOK OPEN means the hook load cell is unserviceable.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook System Description states that the HOOK ARM CAS message indicates that the cargo hook release system is armed, and that HOOK OPEN confirms that the hook is actually open, providing clear status feedback to the crew during external load operations.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook system, indications (p.7-719)

items.question: What is the function of the load cell described in the Cargo Hook System Description?
options: It measures the external load weight and provides this information to the cockpit indication system.
It ensures the hook remains closed by applying a constant clamping force to the load ring.
It limits the maximum hoist speed by sensing cable tension.
It prevents hook opening whenever the load exceeds 1000 kg.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook System Description explains that a load cell is installed to measure the external load weight, and this information is provided to the cockpit indication system so the crew can monitor the weight carried on the hook.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook system, load cell (p.7-720)

items.question: In the Cargo Hook System Description, what operational restriction is given regarding taxiing with the cargo hook installed?
options: Taxiing on unprepared surfaces is prohibited when the cargo hook or sling is installed.
Taxiing is only allowed with the hook installed if the load is less than 500 kg.
Taxiing is unrestricted with the hook installed as long as the hook is empty.
Taxiing is allowed only in calm wind conditions when carrying an external load.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook System Description notes that taxiing on unprepared surfaces is prohibited when the cargo hook or sling is installed, to avoid damaging the hook, sling or airframe.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook system, operational restrictions (p.7-722)

items.question: What is the stated maximum external load for the Cargo Hook system in the System Description?
options: 1500 kg (3307 lb) as maximum external load.
1000 kg (2205 lb) as maximum external load.
2000 kg (4409 lb) as maximum external load.
750 kg (1653 lb) as maximum external load.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook System Description specifies a maximum external load of 1500 kg (approximately 3307 lb) for the standard hook installation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook system, general (p.7-716)

items.question: According to the Cargo Hook Cameras kit description, how are the camera images typically displayed to the crew?
options: As NTSC video on the MFD video page when the camera is selected via the EDCU.
Only on an external mission display in the cabin, not on the flight deck screens.
As still images recorded and replayed after landing.
As synthetic symbology overlaid on the PFD attitude display.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook Cameras kit description explains that the cameras provide NTSC video which can be selected and displayed on the MFD video page using the EDCU, giving the crew a direct view of the hook and load.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook cameras kit (p.7-723)

items.question: What is the main operational advantage of using the cargo hook cameras kit as described in the System Description?
options: It allows the crew to continuously monitor the hook and external load without relying solely on visual lookout from the cockpit windows.
It automatically measures the load centre of gravity and feeds it to the AFCS.
It provides infrared images for night navigation independent of NVG equipment.
It records flight data for maintenance trend monitoring.
items.explanation: The System Description emphasises that the cargo hook cameras kit allows the crew to see the hook and the load on the MFD video page, improving situational awareness during external load operations compared to relying only on direct visual lookout.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook cameras kit (p.7-723)

items.question: In the External Hoist kit description, how is hoist control divided between the pilot and the hoist operator?
options: The pilot has a hoist control switch on the collective grip for basic UP/DOWN control, while the hoist operator uses the hoist control pendant for precise drum control and positioning.
Only the hoist operator can move the hoist, since there is no pilot hoist control provided.
The pilot controls hoist movement exclusively from the overhead OES panel, and the hoist operator has no control pendant.
The hoist may only be controlled through the AFCS in an automatic hover mode.
items.explanation: The External Hoist kit System Description explains that the pilot has a hoist control switch on the collective grip to control UP and DOWN movement, while the hoist operator uses a dedicated hoist pendant with further controls, allowing shared but clearly defined control of hoist movement.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES External hoist kit, controls (p.7-710)

items.question: What is one of the key preflight checks for the Cargo Hook system described in the System Description before external load operations?
options: Verify correct hook operation by commanding an electrical release with no load attached and confirming both hook movement and HOOK OPEN indication.
Check that the hook cameras are recording continuously to the mission recorder before powering the hook.
Verify that the hoist cable is fully extended and retracted three times before any hook operation.
Confirm that the floats are fully inflated and that the cargo hook is locked closed mechanically.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook System Description requires that the crew perform a functional check of the cargo hook before operations, typically by commanding an electrical release with no load attached and confirming correct hook opening and HOOK OPEN indication, to ensure the release system works as intended.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - OES Cargo hook system, preflight checks (p.7-721)

items.question: When engaging an AFCS upper mode from the mode select panel, what does the System Description state about the sequence between arming and capturing a mode?
options: The mode is first shown in white as ARMED when selected, then turns green as it captures and becomes ACTIVE.
The mode immediately appears in green as ACTIVE and later changes to white as the capture is completed.
The mode is always displayed in amber during the entire engagement.
The mode is only displayed after 10 seconds to avoid nuisance annunciations.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description explains that upper modes are first shown in white on the PFD as ARMED when selected, and turn green when they capture and become ACTIVE.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS modes

items.question: According to the AFCS description, what is the primary effect of pressing the AP OFF pushbutton on the cyclic grip once?
options: It arms automatic AP disconnect and requires a second press within the time window to fully disconnect the autopilot.
It immediately disconnects all AFCS functions with no further action required.
It changes the AFCS to basic SAS-only mode without disconnecting upper modes.
It only disconnects yaw control while pitch and roll remain coupled.
items.explanation: The System Description notes that a first press of AP OFF on the cyclic arms the autopilot disconnect logic, and a second press within the specified time disconnects the autopilot, giving the pilot a deliberate two-step action.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS controls

items.question: How does the System Description say the WLVL (wing level) mode behaves when selected in AFCS?
options: It commands the helicopter to roll wings level and holds present heading, overriding other lateral modes with high priority.
It holds the current bank angle and heading until a new mode is selected.
It commands a fixed rate turn to the nearest cardinal heading.
It is only available on the ground to assist taxi turns.
items.explanation: The AFCS section describes WLVL as a high-priority lateral mode that rolls the helicopter wings level and holds heading, overriding existing lateral modes when engaged.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS lateral modes

items.question: What does the System Description state about the GA/TU (Go-Around/Transition Up) button on the collective grip?
options: It commands a go-around flight path or transition-up profile and has priority over other active vertical modes when pressed.
It only arms the go-around mode and requires a second press to command a climb.
It is used solely to test the AFCS on the ground and is inhibited in flight.
It changes the AFCS to basic attitude hold without altering flight path.
items.explanation: The AFCS description notes that the GA/TU button on the collective commands a go-around or transition-up profile and takes priority over existing vertical modes when activated, providing a quick way to establish a safe climb.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS go-around

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what is the function of the ATT pushbutton when upper modes are engaged?
options: It deselects the active upper modes and reverts the AFCS to basic attitude hold while keeping the autopilot channels engaged.
It disconnects the autopilot entirely and returns to full manual control with no attitude hold.
It engages a fixed climb attitude regardless of pilot cyclic input.
It only affects yaw control while pitch and roll modes remain unchanged.
items.explanation: The System Description explains that pressing the ATT pushbutton cancels upper modes and returns the AFCS to basic attitude hold using the engaged autopilot channels, allowing the pilot to quickly simplify the flight director.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS ATT mode

items.question: What does the AFCS description say about using the cyclic 5-way trim switch when flying with upper modes engaged?
options: Small cyclic trim inputs are used to adjust the AFCS reference (such as target attitude or track) without disengaging the mode.
Any use of the trim switch automatically disconnects upper modes and reverts to manual SAS.
The trim switch is inhibited whenever an upper mode is active.
The trim switch only affects yaw and has no effect on pitch or roll when modes are engaged.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description notes that the cyclic trim switch allows the pilot to make small adjustments to the commanded attitude or track in upper modes without disconnecting them, refining the AFCS reference rather than hand-flying.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS trim inputs

items.question: In the AFCS description, what is the recommended pilot action if one AFCS channel fails but the helicopter remains controllable?
options: Continue flight using the remaining AFCS channels, monitoring the associated CAS messages and considering a safe landing as soon as practicable.
Immediately shut down both engines and autorotate to the nearest suitable landing area.
Switch off all AFCS equipment and continue flight using only manual mechanical controls without hydraulic support.
Engage all available upper modes to compensate for the failed channel.
items.explanation: The System Description explains that in the event of a single AFCS channel failure, the remaining channels can continue to support flight, and the crew should monitor annunciations and plan a safe landing, rather than immediately abandoning AFCS use.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS failures

items.question: What is the primary role of the SCAS (Stability and Control Augmentation System) described in the Flight Control System section?
options: To improve short-term stability and damping by providing limited authority control inputs in response to rate and attitude changes.
To provide full autopilot capability including coupled approaches and automatic hover.
To replace the hydraulic servos entirely with electrical actuators.
To control engine power output independently of pilot input.
items.explanation: The Flight Control System description states that SCAS provides limited authority control inputs based on rate and attitude information to improve short-term stability and damping, reducing pilot workload without fully replacing pilot control.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Flight controls and SCAS

items.question: According to the Flight Control System description, how are pilot cyclic and collective inputs transmitted to the main rotor?
options: Through mechanical linkages and mixer units to hydraulic main rotor actuators that then move the swashplate.
Through direct electrical signals from the grips to electric motors on each rotor blade.
Via a cable system that moves trim tabs on the rotor blades only.
By varying engine RPM without using any swashplate movement.
items.explanation: The System Description explains that cyclic and collective inputs are transmitted via mechanical linkages and mixers to hydraulic main rotor actuators, which in turn move the swashplate and change blade pitch.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Flight controls

items.question: What does the Main Rotor System description state about the function of the lead-lag dampers?
options: They control blade lead-lag motion to reduce vibrations and structural loads.
They provide automatic blade de-icing by heating the root area.
They allow the blades to fold for storage without removing them.
They act as backup pitch-change bearings in case of primary bearing failure.
items.explanation: The Main Rotor System description notes that lead-lag dampers are fitted to control the lead-lag motion of the blades, reducing vibration and structural loads on the rotor system.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Main rotor

items.question: In the Tail Rotor System description, what is the purpose of the tail rotor pitch-change mechanism?
options: To vary tail rotor blade pitch in response to pedal inputs, providing yaw control.
To change tail rotor RPM independently of the main rotor.
To feather the tail rotor blades for cruise efficiency.
To automatically trim bank angle during turns.
items.explanation: The Tail Rotor System description explains that the pitch-change mechanism varies tail rotor blade pitch based on pedal inputs, generating the required yaw moments for directional control.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Tail rotor

items.question: According to the Transmission System description, what is the primary role of the main gearbox (MGB)?
options: To reduce the combined engine output speed and transmit torque to the main rotor and tail rotor drive systems.
To store hydraulic fluid for the flight control servos.
To provide electrical power to the AC and DC buses.
To control engine fuel flow through mechanical linkages.
items.explanation: The Transmission System description states that the main gearbox reduces engine output speed and transmits torque to the main rotor and to the tail rotor drive shaft through the intermediate and tail gearboxes.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Transmission

items.question: What is the purpose of the chip detectors described in the Transmission System section?
options: To detect metallic particles in the gearbox oil and alert the crew to possible gear or bearing damage.
To measure oil temperature and control the cooling fan speed.
To sample oil for contamination during scheduled maintenance only.
To indicate oil quantity low conditions in the fuel tanks.
items.explanation: The System Description explains that chip detectors are installed in the gearboxes to detect metallic particles in the oil; when particles bridge the detector, a signal is generated to warn the crew of possible internal damage.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Transmission, chip detection

items.question: According to the Transmission System description, what is the function of the oil cooler fan system?
options: To maintain gearbox oil temperature within limits by forcing air through the oil cooler.
To ventilate the cabin by extracting hot air from the roof.
To cool the avionics racks in the nose compartment.
To provide cooling air for the engine bleed air ducts.
items.explanation: The Transmission System section states that an oil cooler and fan system is provided to maintain gearbox oil temperature within prescribed limits by forcing air through the cooler matrix.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Transmission, lubrication and cooling

items.question: In the Engine System description, what is the primary role of the FADEC for each engine?
options: To provide full authority digital control of fuel flow and engine parameters throughout the operating envelope.
To manage the electrical power distribution from the generators.
To automatically control cabin temperature and ventilation.
To activate the fire extinguishing system in case of overtemperature.
items.explanation: The Engine section explains that each PW210 engine is controlled by a FADEC which provides full authority digital control of fuel flow and engine parameters in all phases of operation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine, FADEC

items.question: According to the Engine System description, what is the function of the ENGINE mode select (such as IDLE/FLIGHT) on the overhead panel?
options: It selects the desired operating mode for the engines, such as IDLE or FLIGHT, and commands the FADEC to schedule fuel accordingly.
It directly opens and closes the engine fuel shutoff valves without FADEC involvement.
It is used only to control the APU and has no effect on the main engines.
It changes the electrical system configuration between single and dual generator mode.
items.explanation: The Engine System section describes that the engine mode select controls (IDLE/FLIGHT) command the FADEC to schedule fuel for the selected operating mode, determining engine power settings appropriate for idle or flight.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine controls

items.question: What does the Engine System description state about automatic engine protection during start?
options: The FADEC monitors start parameters and will automatically abort the start if limits such as temperature or rotor speed are exceeded.
There is no automatic protection; the pilot must manually abort the start by closing the fuel shutoff valve.
Protection is only provided for high oil pressure and not for temperature.
Automatic start protection is available only when using external power.
items.explanation: The Engine System description notes that the FADEC monitors engine parameters during start and can automatically abort the start if certain limits are exceeded, protecting the engine from damage.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine start protection

items.question: In the Fuel System description, what is the function of the crossfeed capability between tanks?
options: To allow fuel from one side to be supplied to both engines in case of a pump or tank problem.
To permit fuel jettison overboard from either tank.
To supply fuel to the cabin heater independently of the engines.
To refill the tanks automatically from an external fuel bladder.
items.explanation: The Fuel System section explains that crossfeed allows fuel from one side to be supplied to both engines, giving flexibility in case of a fuel pump or tank problem on one side.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system

items.question: According to the Fuel System description, how is fuel quantity typically displayed to the crew?
options: On the fuel synoptic page and on dedicated fuel quantity indications on the MFD/PFD.
Only on a mechanical gauge in the refuelling panel.
By a single low fuel warning light when total fuel is below a fixed value.
As a percentage of maximum weight on the AFCS page only.
items.explanation: The Fuel System description notes that fuel quantity is displayed on the fuel synoptic page and by dedicated indications on the displays, allowing the crew to monitor quantity in each tank.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel indications

items.question: What is the main purpose of the Engine Oil System described in the System Description?
options: To lubricate and cool engine bearings and gears and to provide hydraulic power for some engine actuators.
To supply de-icing fluid to the engine intakes.
To pressurise the fuel tanks during high altitude flight.
To provide backup hydraulic pressure for the main rotor servos.
items.explanation: The Engine Oil System description explains that engine oil lubricates and cools engine bearings and gears and may drive some engine actuators, ensuring reliable engine operation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine oil system

items.question: According to the Electrical Power System description, what is the normal source of DC power in flight?
options: The main engine-driven generators feeding the DC buses via the power distribution system.
The battery alone, with generators used only on the ground.
An external power cart connected to the ground power receptacle.
Permanent magnet alternators that are independent of the engines.
items.explanation: The Electrical Power System description states that the engine-driven generators are the normal sources of DC power in flight, supplying the DC buses through the distribution system.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power, normal operation

items.question: What is the primary purpose of the main battery described in the Electrical Power System section?
options: To provide power for engine starting and to supply essential loads in case of generator failure.
To supply all cabin lighting continuously during flight.
To power the hoist and cargo hook systems only.
To drive the rotor brake motor when engines are shut down.
items.explanation: The Electrical Power System description notes that the battery is used primarily for engine start and as a backup source for essential loads if the generators fail.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power, battery

items.question: According to the Hydraulics System description, what is the purpose of having two main hydraulic systems?
options: To provide redundancy so that flight controls remain powered if one hydraulic system fails.
To allow one system to be used for the cabin doors and one for the landing gear only.
To alternate operation between flights to reduce wear.
To power the hoist from one system and the cargo hook from the other.
items.explanation: The Hydraulics section explains that two independent main hydraulic systems are provided so that if one system fails, the other can continue to power the flight control servos, giving redundancy.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system

items.question: What is the function of the EHPS (Electrical Hydraulic Pump System) mentioned in the Hydraulics description?
options: To provide backup hydraulic pressure on the ground or in flight when an engine-driven pump is not available.
To power only the landing gear retraction mechanism.
To supply hydraulic pressure exclusively to the rotor brake caliper.
To drive the cargo hook release mechanism.
items.explanation: The Hydraulics description states that the EHPS can supply hydraulic pressure as a backup when an engine-driven pump is unavailable, such as during ground checks or certain failure conditions.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system, EHPS

items.question: In the Ice and Rain Protection System description, what is the main purpose of the windshield heating?
options: To prevent ice formation and remove misting on the pilot and copilot windshields.
To keep cabin temperature comfortable for passengers.
To protect the avionics racks from condensation.
To heat the engine intakes only.
items.explanation: The Ice and Rain Protection section explains that windshield heating is provided to prevent ice formation and remove misting on the windshields, ensuring adequate visibility.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Ice and rain protection, windshield heat

items.question: According to the Engine Air Intake System description, what is the purpose of the anti-ice system at the engine inlets?
options: To prevent ice accumulation at the engine air intakes and protect against engine power loss.
To increase engine power by heating the intake air for better combustion.
To reduce cabin noise by dampening airflow.
To provide bleed air for the cabin heating system.
items.explanation: The Engine Air Intake System section notes that an anti-ice system is provided at the engine inlets to prevent ice accumulation that could otherwise lead to engine power loss or compressor stall.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine air intake and anti-ice

items.question: In the Fire Detection and Extinguishing System description, what areas are typically protected by fire detectors on the AW169?
options: The engine compartments and the APU compartment if installed.
Only the cabin and baggage compartments.
The main rotor hub and blade roots.
The landing gear bays and tail boom.
items.explanation: The Fire Detection and Extinguishing section describes fire detectors installed in the engine compartments and, if fitted, in the APU compartment to detect fire in those areas.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fire detection

items.question: According to the Fire Extinguishing System description, how are the engine fire bottles normally discharged?
options: By pressing the appropriate guarded FIRE EXT pushbutton after pulling the associated T-handle or activating the engine fire control.
By cycling the engine mode selector from FLIGHT to IDLE three times.
Automatically whenever the fire detectors sense a temperature above a preset value.
By operating the rotor brake lever to the emergency position.
items.explanation: The Fire Extinguishing System section explains that the crew discharges an engine fire bottle by operating the guarded FIRE EXT pushbutton after the engine fire control has been actuated, directing extinguishing agent into the affected compartment.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fire extinguishing

items.question: In the Environmental Control System description, what is the primary function of the ECS?
options: To provide conditioned air for cabin heating, cooling and ventilation.
To supply hydraulic pressure to the flight control servos.
To operate the cargo hook release.
To control the main rotor speed during autorotation.
items.explanation: The Environmental Control System (ECS) description states that its primary function is to provide conditioned air for cabin heating, cooling and ventilation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Environmental Control System

items.question: According to the Lighting System description, what is the purpose of the emergency lighting system in the cabin?
options: To provide illumination for evacuation routes and exits in case of a loss of normal electrical power.
To light up the cargo hook area during external load operations.
To illuminate the main rotor disk for ground crew at night.
To provide decorative mood lighting for passengers.
items.explanation: The Lighting System description notes that emergency lights are installed in the cabin to illuminate evacuation routes and exits if normal electrical power is lost, aiding emergency egress.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Lighting, emergency lights

items.question: According to the Engine System description, what is the main purpose of the engine power rating indications (such as MCP, TO, OEI ratings) on the displays?
options: To show the crew the current engine operating range and available power margin so that power can be managed within limits.
To indicate only fuel flow and oil pressure during engine start.
To provide backup attitude information in case of PFD failure.
To control the FADEC manually by selecting the desired rating.
items.explanation: The Engine System description explains that engine power rating indications show which rating is in use (for example MCP or OEI) and the associated limits, helping the crew manage power within the approved operating ranges.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine indications

items.question: In the FADEC description, what does the automatic matching function between engines primarily provide during normal twin-engine operation?
options: It keeps engine outputs synchronised so that torque sharing remains balanced between the two engines.
It alternates which engine carries all the load every five minutes.
It shuts one engine down automatically when torque is low.
It disconnects the transmission from the engines in cruise flight.
items.explanation: The FADEC section notes that an automatic matching function is used to keep engines closely matched, so that torque sharing is balanced and asymmetric thrust is avoided in normal twin-engine operation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine, FADEC functions

items.question: According to the Fuel System description, what is the consequence of switching OFF one of the main fuel pumps on a side in normal conditions?
options: The remaining pump on that side continues to supply fuel, and the crew will see the associated pump indication change but no immediate engine flameout.
The engine on that side will immediately flame out because crossfeed is not possible.
Both engines will automatically revert to idle power.
The fuel quantity indication for that side is removed from the display.
items.explanation: The Fuel System description explains that each side has multiple fuel pumps; switching one pump OFF leaves the remaining pump to supply fuel, and the change is indicated on the synoptic without causing an immediate engine flameout in normal conditions.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system, pumps

items.question: In the Hydraulic System description, what is the role of the priority valves when system pressure becomes low?
options: They ensure that flight control servos retain hydraulic supply by shedding lower priority users when pressure is limited.
They transfer hydraulic fluid from one reservoir to the other to equalise quantity.
They automatically shut down both engines to protect the pumps.
They open bypasses so that hydraulic pressure drops to zero quickly.
items.explanation: The Hydraulic System section describes priority valves that protect essential users such as flight controls: if pressure decreases, the valves limit supply to non-essential users so that the servos remain powered as long as possible.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system, priority valves

items.question: According to the Electrical Power System description, what is the normal crew action if one generator fails in flight while loads remain within limits?
options: Monitor the remaining generator load and continue flight on the single generator, reducing non-essential loads if necessary.
Immediately switch off all avionics and land at the nearest site.
Select external power on the ground power switch while still in flight.
Pull all generator circuit breakers to avoid further malfunction.
items.explanation: The Electrical Power System description explains that following a single generator failure, the remaining generator can normally supply the essential loads; the crew should monitor generator load and, if necessary, reduce non-essential loads while continuing to a suitable landing.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power, single generator operation

items.question: In the Environmental Control System description, how is cockpit and cabin temperature normally adjusted by the crew?
options: By using the ECS temperature controls to select the desired temperature, after which the system automatically mixes hot and cold air to achieve it.
By opening and closing the side windows only, since no ECS temperature control is provided.
By changing engine power setting, which is the only way to control bleed air temperature.
By switching the battery OFF to reduce electrical heating in the cabin.
items.explanation: The ECS description states that cockpit and cabin temperature are normally controlled with dedicated ECS temperature selectors; the system then adjusts hot and cold air mixing to reach the selected temperature automatically.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Environmental Control System, controls

items.question: According to the Fire Detection System description, what is the crew's first indication of an engine fire from the detection loops?
options: An engine FIRE warning with associated lights and aural alert triggered by the detection loops.
A gradual rise in indicated oil temperature without any lights.
A change in rotor RPM indication on the PFD only.
A CAS advisory labelled ENGINE HOT with no aural tone.
items.explanation: The Fire Detection System description explains that temperature-sensitive loops trigger an engine FIRE warning, associated lights and an aural alert when a fire is detected, providing the crew with a clear first indication.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fire detection, indications

items.question: In the Ice and Rain Protection System description, what is the recommended use of windshield wipers at higher speeds?
options: They are intended primarily for use at low airspeeds; at higher speeds, rain repellant and windshield heat are preferred.
They should be used continuously at maximum speed in all flight conditions.
They must never be used in rain because they can scratch the windshield.
They are only for ground use during maintenance.
