items.explanation: The Ice and Rain Protection section notes that windshield wipers are mainly intended for low-speed operation; at higher airspeeds, windshield heat and, if installed, rain repellent are preferred methods to maintain visibility.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Ice and rain protection, windshield wipers

items.question: According to the Lighting System description, what is the purpose of the NVG-compatible cockpit lighting?
options: To provide sufficient instrument illumination without degrading the performance of night vision goggles.
To increase the brightness of all indicators to maximum for night operations.
To flash all annunciators during NVG approaches.
To light only the overhead panel while the rest of the cockpit remains dark.
items.explanation: The Lighting System description explains that NVG-compatible lighting is designed to illuminate instruments and controls while remaining compatible with night vision goggles, avoiding glare and blooming that could reduce NVG effectiveness.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Lighting, NVG

items.question: In the Avionics System description, what is the main role of the integrated display system (PFD/MFD) for the crew?
options: To combine flight, engine and system information into reconfigurable displays that support normal and abnormal operations.
To store maintenance procedures for ground technicians only.
To replace all radio communication equipment.
To control the rotor brake and landing gear directly.
items.explanation: The Avionics System description states that the integrated display system presents primary flight information, engine parameters and system synoptics on reconfigurable PFD/MFD screens, providing the crew with the information needed for normal and abnormal operations.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Avionics, display system

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what is the primary function of the IAS (indicated airspeed) mode when engaged?
options: To maintain the selected airspeed by adjusting pitch/attitude while allowing the pilot to change the reference with the IAS selector.
To hold the current heading regardless of wind drift.
To maintain a constant rate of climb independent of airspeed.
To automatically capture and hold a selected radar altitude.
items.explanation: The AFCS section describes IAS mode as a speed-hold function: when engaged, the AFCS adjusts pitch to maintain the selected indicated airspeed, with the pilot able to change the reference using the IAS control.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, IAS mode

items.question: In the AFCS description, what does the ALT (altitude hold) mode do when it becomes active?
options: It maintains the helicopter at the captured barometric altitude until a new altitude or vertical mode is selected.
It maintains a constant vertical speed regardless of altitude.
It commands a continuous climb to the service ceiling.
It maintains current radar altitude only below 200 ft.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description explains that once ALT mode captures, the AFCS holds the barometric altitude at the point of capture, keeping the helicopter at that altitude until another mode or reference is selected.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, ALT mode

items.question: According to the AFCS description, what is the purpose of the VS (vertical speed) mode?
options: To hold a pilot-selected rate of climb or descent until another vertical mode is chosen or the reference is changed.
To maintain a constant IAS regardless of climb or descent.
To keep the helicopter at a fixed radar altitude.
To synchronise engine torque between the two engines.
items.explanation: The AFCS description states that VS mode allows the pilot to select a desired vertical speed; the AFCS then adjusts pitch to maintain that rate of climb or descent until another vertical mode is selected or the VS reference is altered.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, VS mode

items.question: In the AFCS description, what is the main operational use of the HDG (heading) mode?
options: To maintain the selected heading by commanding yaw and roll as needed once the mode is engaged.
To keep the helicopter aligned with the current track regardless of wind.
To hold the last selected course from a VOR or GPS.
To automatically follow the flight plan loaded in the FMS.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description describes HDG mode as a basic lateral mode that maintains the selected heading; when engaged, the AFCS commands yaw/roll to keep the helicopter on that heading until the pilot selects a new heading or mode.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, HDG mode

items.question: According to the AFCS/NAV integration description, what is the primary function of the NAV mode?
options: To couple the AFCS to a selected navigation source so that it tracks the programmed course or flight plan from that sensor.
To maintain current magnetic heading and ignore all navigation inputs.
To hold the helicopter over a fixed geographic point using only radar altitude.
To provide automatic engine synchronisation during climb.
items.explanation: The System Description explains that NAV mode couples the AFCS to a selected navigation source (such as FMS or VOR) so that the helicopter tracks the programmed course or flight plan, providing lateral guidance based on that sensor.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, NAV mode

items.question: According to the AFCS hover/low speed description, what is the main purpose of the HOV (hover) mode?
options: To maintain a stabilised hover by holding position and height within the defined AFCS envelope when engaged in suitable conditions.
To command a climb to a pre-set altitude while ignoring lateral movement.
To maintain current IAS and heading in cruise flight.
To automatically execute a full approach to hover from any point on the flight plan.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description notes that HOV mode is used in low-speed/hover operations to stabilise the helicopter in hover, maintaining position and height within the mode's envelope when conditions and sensors permit.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, HOV mode

items.question: In the AFCS radar height related functions, what is the role of the RHT (radar height) mode?
options: To maintain a selected radar altitude above the surface, typically used in low level or approach operations.
To maintain a selected barometric altitude irrespective of terrain.
To hold a fixed vertical speed referenced to the radar altimeter.
To provide only aural alerts without controlling the flight path.
items.explanation: The AFCS description explains that when RHT mode is engaged the AFCS uses radar altitude as the controlled variable, maintaining the selected height above surface within the limits described for low altitude operations.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, RHT mode

items.question: According to the AFCS approach modes description, what is the primary function of the APP (approach) mode when coupled to a precision or non-precision approach?
options: To provide lateral and vertical guidance along the selected approach path by following the navigation and glideslope/vertical guidance signals.
To hold heading while the pilot manually tracks the localiser only.
To climb to the missed approach altitude immediately after selection.
To disengage all other modes and leave only SCAS active.
items.explanation: The AFCS section states that APP mode is used to couple the helicopter to instrument approaches, providing both lateral and vertical guidance based on the selected navigation and glideslope or equivalent vertical guidance signals.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, APP mode

items.question: In the AFCS deceleration functions description, what is the main use of the DCL (deceleration) mode?
options: To command a controlled deceleration from forward flight towards a hover or low speed while managing pitch and, where applicable, collective.
To maintain a constant IAS during climb or descent.
To synchronise rotor speed with engine torque.
To automatically initiate a go-around when the approach path is unstable.
items.explanation: The AFCS description explains that DCL mode is used to achieve a managed deceleration profile, reducing speed towards a defined low-speed or hover condition while the AFCS commands pitch (and, for some configurations, collective) according to the programmed law.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, DCL mode

items.question: According to the AFCS collective/engine protection description, what is the purpose of the OEI/ALT capture logic during engine-out operations?
options: To coordinate AFCS collective commands with OEI power limits so that the helicopter can capture and maintain a safe altitude or profile without exceeding OEI limits.
To shut down the remaining engine automatically after a fixed time.
To force the helicopter into autorotation regardless of pilot input.
To disable all AFCS vertical modes whenever OEI is detected.
items.explanation: The AFCS System Description notes that specific logic coordinates collective control with OEI power limits so that capture of a selected altitude or profile can be achieved without exceeding OEI ratings, supporting engine-out management.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS, OEI/ALT capture

items.question: According to the Main Rotor and Rotor Brake description, how is the rotor brake intended to be used by the crew in normal operation?
options: Only on the ground to stop the rotor after engine shutdown or at low power, never in flight.
In flight to reduce rotor RPM quickly during descents.
At any time to assist yaw control when pedals are ineffective.
As the primary method of securing the helicopter on sloping ground.
items.explanation: The System Description for the rotor brake states that it is provided to stop rotor rotation on the ground after engine shutdown or at low power settings and is not intended for in-flight use.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Main rotor and rotor brake

items.question: In the Transmission System description, what is the primary function of the main gearbox (MGB) oil cooling system?
options: To maintain MGB oil temperature within the prescribed limits by circulating oil through a cooler and associated fans or heat exchangers.
To provide emergency hydraulic pressure to the flight controls in case of pump failure.
To cool only the tail rotor gearbox while the main gearbox is air cooled.
To supply pressurised oil to the engines for lubrication during autorotation.
items.explanation: The Transmission System section explains that the MGB oil cooling system circulates oil through a cooler, assisted by airflow and fans or heat exchangers as installed, in order to keep gearbox oil temperature within specified limits.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Transmission, oil cooling

items.question: According to the Engine System description, what is one of the main functions of the FADEC during engine start?
options: To automatically schedule fuel flow and ignition to keep key parameters within limits and protect against abnormal start conditions.
To mechanically open the fuel shutoff valve by direct cable linkage.
To disengage the starter immediately when the pilot releases the start switch, without any automatic logic.
To command rotor brake application if rotor speed increases too quickly.
items.explanation: The Engine System description notes that the FADEC monitors engine parameters during start, automatically controlling fuel and ignition and providing protections to keep the start within defined limits.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine, FADEC and start sequence

items.question: In the Fuel System description, what is the primary role of the transfer/boost pumps in the main tanks?
options: To supply pressurised fuel from the tanks to the engine-driven pumps and help prevent vapour formation or starvation.
To circulate fuel only for cabin heating purposes.
To transfer fuel from the engines back into the tanks during descent.
To provide hydraulic pressure to the landing gear actuators.
items.explanation: The Fuel System section explains that electric transfer or boost pumps in the main tanks provide a pressurised fuel supply to the engine-driven pumps, improving reliability and reducing the risk of vapour lock or starvation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system, pumps

items.question: According to the Hydraulic System description, what is the main purpose of the Emergency Hydraulic Pump System (EHPS) when installed?
options: To provide an alternate source of hydraulic pressure to selected flight control servos following loss of normal system pressure.
To cool hydraulic fluid during extended ground operations only.
To operate the landing gear doors during normal cycles.
To pressurise the fuel system when all engine-driven pumps are offline.
items.explanation: The Hydraulic System description states that the EHPS, where installed, is designed to supply hydraulic pressure to essential flight control users when normal hydraulic pressure is not available, thereby preserving controllability.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system, EHPS

items.question: In the Engine Oil System description, what is the primary purpose of the engine oil cooler?
options: To maintain engine oil temperature within limits by routing oil through a heat exchanger that uses air or another medium for cooling.
To supply additional fuel to the engines during high power operations.
To provide backup hydraulic pressure to the tail rotor servo.
To warm the cabin air directly in cold conditions.
items.explanation: The Engine Oil System section states that engine oil is circulated through a cooler to keep its temperature within prescribed limits, using airflow or another cooling medium depending on installation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine, oil system

items.question: According to the Ice and Rain Protection description, what is the main function of the engine air inlet anti-ice system?
options: To prevent ice accumulation at the engine intakes by supplying heated air or using other anti-ice means as described.
To cool the engine in high temperature conditions by directing cold air to the intakes.
To provide backup cabin ventilation when the ECS fails.
To keep the rotor brake components free of ice.
items.explanation: The System Description explains that the engine air inlet anti-ice system is intended to prevent ice build-up at the engine intakes, using heated air or other means described for the installation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Ice and rain protection, engine intake anti-ice

items.question: In the Environmental Control System description, what is the purpose of the recirculation fans when installed?
options: To improve cabin airflow and temperature homogeneity by recirculating cabin air through the ECS.
To provide emergency pressurisation of the cabin at high altitude.
To ventilate only the avionics bay without affecting cabin comfort.
To extract fuel vapours from the tanks during refuelling.
items.explanation: The ECS section describes recirculation fans as devices that enhance cabin airflow and help maintain even temperature distribution by recirculating cabin air through the environmental control system.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Environmental Control System, recirculation

items.question: According to the Electrical Power System description, what is the role of the battery in normal operations when generators are online?
options: To provide stabilisation and backup for the DC network while normally remaining charged by the generators.
To supply all AC power to the main buses continuously.
To operate only the cabin lighting when the engines are shut down.
To control the main rotor speed directly when the FADEC is offline.
items.explanation: The Electrical Power System description notes that when generators are online the battery remains connected to the DC network, acting as a stabilising and backup source while being maintained charged.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power, battery

items.question: In the Avionics/Displays description, what is the primary function of the reversionary mode for the cockpit display system?
options: To allow essential flight and engine information to be shown on remaining displays if one screen fails.
To switch all displays off automatically in the event of a failure.
To display only maintenance pages after a screen failure.
To transfer control of the displays to the rear cabin screens.
items.explanation: The cockpit display system description explains that a reversionary mode permits essential flight and engine data to be presented on the remaining screens when one display becomes unavailable, maintaining required information for the crew.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Avionics, display system reversionary mode

items.question: According to the Engine System description, what is the main purpose of the ENGINE MODE selector in normal operations?
options: To select the appropriate engine operating mode (such as IDLE or FLIGHT) so that the FADEC can apply the correct control laws.
To directly control rotor RPM mechanically without FADEC involvement.
To switch the hydraulic system between normal and emergency modes.
To enable or disable the landing gear indication system.
items.explanation: The Engine System description explains that the engine mode selector is used to choose the required engine operating mode, allowing the FADEC to apply the corresponding control laws and schedules.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine, mode selector

items.question: In the FADEC description, what is one of the protections provided during engine operation?
options: Automatic limitation of engine parameters to prevent exceedance of specified limits.
Automatic extension and retraction of the landing gear based on airspeed.
Continuous adjustment of rotor blade pitch for vibration reduction only.
Automatic activation of the hoist system during takeoff.
items.explanation: The FADEC section states that the digital control system includes limiters designed to prevent certain engine parameters from exceeding their permissible values, providing engine protection.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine, FADEC protections

items.question: According to the Fuel System description, how is crossfeed or interconnection between the main tanks generally managed in normal operation?
options: By system logic and pilot-operated valves that allow fuel balancing or crossfeed according to the procedure.
By automatically transferring all fuel to one side at low fuel states.
By gravity alone with no valves provided.
By opening electrical breakers on the fuel pumps.
items.explanation: The Fuel System section describes that interconnection and crossfeed between tanks is managed by valves and, where applicable, automatic logic; the pilot can open or close crossfeed in accordance with procedures for balancing or abnormal conditions.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system, crossfeed

items.question: In the Electrical Power System description, what is the typical crew action if both generators are lost but the battery remains available?
options: Reduce electrical load to essential items and monitor battery time while continuing towards a suitable landing site.
Immediately shut down both engines to preserve battery life.
Switch on all non-essential lights to confirm the failure.
Open all generator and battery circuit breakers to avoid further damage.
items.explanation: The Electrical Power System section notes that following loss of both generators, the crew should shed non-essential loads and use the remaining battery capacity to power essential equipment while planning a landing.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power, dual generator loss

items.question: According to the Hydraulic System description, what is the normal indication to the crew that a hydraulic system has lost pressure?
options: Associated caution or warning indications and hydraulic pressure readings showing a drop below normal limits.
A change in cabin temperature with no cockpit indications.
An automatic extension of the landing gear without any lights.
Loss of all electrical power with no hydraulic indications.
items.explanation: The Hydraulic System section explains that loss of pressure is shown by the associated pressure indication and by caution or warning annunciations, alerting the crew to the degraded system.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system, indications

items.question: In the Main Rotor System description, what is the purpose of the lead-lag dampers?
options: To control lead-lag motion of the blades and reduce rotor-induced vibrations.
To provide primary pitch control of each blade.
To lock the blades in position when the rotor is at high RPM.
To supply hydraulic pressure to the flight control servos.
items.explanation: The Main Rotor System section states that lead-lag dampers are installed to control the in-plane motion of the blades and help reduce vibrations transmitted to the airframe.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Main rotor, dampers

items.question: According to the Tail Rotor and Drive System description, what is the role of the intermediate and tail gearboxes?
options: To transmit power and change drive direction from the main gearbox to the tail rotor.
To store hydraulic fluid for the tail rotor servo only.
To provide emergency electrical power when the main generators fail.
To act as fuel reservoirs for the auxiliary tanks.
items.explanation: The Tail Rotor and Drive System section explains that the intermediate and tail gearboxes change the direction of drive and transfer torque along the tail rotor drive system to the tail rotor head.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Tail rotor and drive

items.question: In the Fire Detection and Extinguishing System description, what is the normal crew action when an engine FIRE warning is confirmed?
options: Carry out the engine fire procedure which includes closing the fuel supply and arming/discharging the appropriate fire extinguishing bottle as specified.
Immediately increase power on the affected engine to clear the warning.
Switch off all cockpit lighting and wait for the warning to extinguish.
Open the cabin doors to ventilate the compartment while continuing flight.
items.explanation: The Fire Detection and Extinguishing System section provides a procedure for an engine FIRE warning which includes confirming the affected engine, closing its fuel supply and, when required, discharging the extinguishing agent.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fire detection and extinguishing

items.question: According to the Environmental Control System description, what is the main purpose of the cockpit demist function?
options: To supply conditioned air to the windscreen and side windows to prevent misting and improve visibility.
To cool the avionics bay during high outside air temperatures.
To provide fresh air to the baggage compartment only.
To remove smoke from the engine bay in case of fire.
items.explanation: The ECS section explains that cockpit demist directs conditioned air towards the windscreen and side windows to prevent fogging and maintain clear outside visibility.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Environmental Control System, demist

items.question: In the Lighting System description, what is the purpose of the emergency lighting system?
options: To provide basic cabin and exit illumination in the event of loss of normal electrical power.
To illuminate the rotor blades during all night operations.
To provide coloured mood lighting in the passenger cabin.
To mark only the hoist operator's station during external load missions.
items.explanation: The Lighting System description states that the emergency lighting is intended to provide essential illumination of the cabin and exits if normal power is lost, assisting evacuation and orientation.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Lighting, emergency lighting

items.question: According to the Flight Controls System description, what is the function of the mixing unit in the control system?
options: To combine pilot control inputs into appropriate movements of the main rotor servos.
To mix hydraulic fluid between systems 1 and 2.
To blend fuel from different tanks before delivery to the engines.
To combine electrical power from the generators and battery.
items.explanation: The Flight Controls System section describes a mixing unit that converts pilot control movements into the correct combination of servo inputs for the main rotor system.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Flight controls, mixing unit

items.question: In the SCAS (Stability and Control Augmentation System) description, what is one of its primary purposes?
options: To improve helicopter stability and handling by applying small automatic control inputs.
To automatically deploy the landing gear based on airspeed.
To start and stop the engines without pilot input.
To command automatic hoist operation during external load missions.
items.explanation: The SCAS description states that the system applies small automatic inputs to the controls to reduce pilot workload and improve stability, particularly in turbulence.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS/SCAS

items.question: According to the Pitot-Static and Air Data System description, why are multiple pitot and static sources provided?
options: To provide redundancy and allow comparison between sources for reliable airspeed and altitude information.
To supply fuel pressure to the engines.
To cool the avionics racks by blowing air through them.
To provide hydraulic pressure to the rotor brake.
items.explanation: The Pitot-Static and Air Data System section explains that multiple air data sources are installed to provide redundancy and permit cross-checking, supporting reliable indications and failure detection.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Pitot-static and air data

items.question: In the Ice and Rain Protection description, what is the primary use of windshield wipers (where installed)?
options: To clear rain from the pilot windscreens to maintain adequate external visibility.
To remove structural ice from the rotor blades.
To de-fog the internal surface of the side windows.
To remove snow from the tail boom.
items.explanation: The Ice and Rain Protection section notes that windshield wipers are provided to clear rain from the pilot windscreen areas and thereby maintain visibility.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Ice and rain protection, windshield wipers

items.question: According to the Oxygen System description (where installed), what is its main purpose?
options: To provide supplemental oxygen to crew and passengers when required by altitude or procedures.
To pressurise the hydraulic reservoirs during cold weather.
To cool the avionics by circulating oxygen through the racks.
To inflate the emergency floats during ditching.
items.explanation: The Oxygen System section states that the system is intended to supply supplemental oxygen to crew and passengers when the flight profile or regulations require its use.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Oxygen system

items.question: In the Cabin and Doors description, what is the purpose of the emergency exits and jettisonable windows?
options: To provide additional escape routes for occupants in an emergency when normal exits are unusable.
To allow routine baggage loading through the cockpit.
To ventilate the cabin during normal operations only.
To access the engine bay for maintenance in flight.
items.explanation: The Cabin and Doors section explains that dedicated emergency exits and jettisonable windows are provided to give alternative escape routes for occupants if normal exits cannot be used.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Cabin, doors and emergency exits

items.question: According to the External Lights description, what is the primary purpose of the anti-collision lights?
options: To enhance the helicopter's conspicuity to other airspace users during flight and on the ground.
To illuminate the cabin for passenger comfort.
To provide map reading light for the pilot.
To mark the location of the hoist operator at night.
items.explanation: The External Lights section describes anti-collision lights as high-intensity lights intended to make the helicopter more visible to others, improving collision avoidance.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Lighting, anti-collision

items.question: In the Avionics description, what is the main function of the flight management system (FMS) where installed?
options: To assist with navigation, performance calculations and route management.
To control hydraulic pressure to the main rotor servos.
To operate the hoist and cargo hook systems automatically.
To provide emergency electrical power when generators fail.
items.explanation: The Avionics section notes that the flight management system integrates navigation sensors and databases to support route planning, navigation and, where applicable, performance calculations.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Avionics, FMS

items.question: According to the Communications System description, what is the primary use of the audio control panels?
options: To allow crew members to select and control audio from radios, intercom and warning systems.
To adjust the rotor RPM.
To change the hydraulic system operating mode.
To set the cabin temperature.
items.explanation: The Communications System description explains that audio control panels permit each crew member to choose which communication and navigation audio sources are heard and to adjust their levels.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Communications, audio control

items.question: In the Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) or equivalent display description, what is one of its main purposes?
options: To present engine and system parameters and alert messages in an integrated format for the crew.
To control the movement of the hoist hook.
To adjust the tension of the tail rotor drive shaft.
To manage the helicopter's fuel loading on the ground.
items.explanation: The indication and alerting system description states that engine and system parameters as well as alerts are displayed on dedicated pages, allowing the crew to monitor helicopter status and respond to warnings and cautions.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Indicating and alerting

items.question: According to the Hoist System description, what is the primary purpose of the hoist overload protection?
options: To prevent loads exceeding specified limits from being lifted, protecting the hoist and structure.
To prevent the hoist from operating at low temperatures.
To ensure the hoist always operates at maximum speed.
To automatically jettison the load whenever the helicopter turns.
items.explanation: The Hoist System section describes overload protection as a feature designed to prevent excessive loads from being lifted, thereby protecting the hoist equipment and airframe attachment points.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hoist system, overload protection

items.question: In the Cargo Hook System description, what is the function of the emergency release?
options: To allow the crew to jettison the external load quickly in an emergency.
To reduce rotor RPM to idle.
To deploy the emergency floats automatically.
To shut down both engines.
items.explanation: The Cargo Hook System description explains that an emergency release provides a rapid means of jettisoning the external load if required for safety.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Cargo hook, emergency release

items.question: According to the Landing Gear description, what is the primary purpose of the weight-on-wheels (WOW) switches?
options: To signal on-ground or in-flight status to various aircraft systems.
To measure fuel quantity in the main tanks.
To adjust rotor blade pitch automatically.
To control cabin temperature based on outside air temperature.
items.explanation: The Landing Gear and systems integration description notes that WOW switches provide signals used by several systems to distinguish ground from flight conditions, affecting logic such as warnings and protections.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Landing gear, WOW

items.question: In the Fuel System description, what is the purpose of fuel filters in the supply line to the engines?
options: To remove contaminants from the fuel before it reaches engine components.
To regulate cabin temperature by heating the fuel.
To pressurise the hydraulic system.
To provide backup lubrication oil to the gearbox.
items.explanation: The Fuel System section states that filters are fitted in the fuel supply to trap contamination and protect the engine fuel system components.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Fuel system, filters

items.question: According to the Engine Oil System description, what is one normal crew response to an engine oil pressure low indication?
options: Refer to the relevant procedure which may include reducing power on the affected engine and considering shutdown if the condition persists.
Immediately increase power on the affected engine to restore pressure.
Switch off all electrical systems to preserve oil.
Ignore the indication if temperature remains normal.
items.explanation: The Engine Oil System section links low oil pressure indications to specific procedures, typically involving confirmation, power reduction on the affected engine and possible shutdown according to the checklist.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Engine, oil pressure low

items.question: In the Transmission System description, what is the function of chip detectors?
options: To detect metallic particles in the lubrication oil and provide an indication of possible component wear.
To measure hydraulic fluid temperature.
To monitor cabin humidity.
To detect ice accretion on the rotor blades.
items.explanation: The Transmission System section explains that chip detectors installed in gearboxes sense metallic particles in the oil, providing early warning of component wear or damage.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Transmission, chip detectors

items.question: According to the Hydraulic System description, what is the purpose of priority valves?
options: To ensure that hydraulic pressure is maintained to essential users before supplying non-essential users.
To prioritise fuel flow to one engine over the other.
To give electrical power priority to the cabin lighting.
To keep the landing gear extended at all times.
items.explanation: The Hydraulic System section states that priority valves are used to maintain pressure to essential services such as flight controls before supplying less critical users.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Hydraulic system, priority valves

items.question: In the Electrical System description, what is the normal function of the external power receptacle?
options: To allow connection of an external power source for ground operations or engine start.
To provide a point for refuelling the helicopter.
To attach the cargo hook equipment.
To connect the rotor brake system to ground air supply.
items.explanation: The Electrical System section notes that an external power receptacle permits the helicopter to be powered from an external source, supporting ground operations and starts without using the battery excessively.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Electrical power, external power

items.question: According to the Environmental Control System description, what is one purpose of the cabin temperature control?
options: To allow the crew to select and maintain a comfortable cabin temperature for occupants.
To control the fuel temperature in the main tanks.
To cool the engine oil directly.
To adjust the tail rotor gearbox temperature.
items.explanation: The ECS section describes temperature control as providing means for the crew to regulate cabin temperature within a comfortable range for crew and passengers.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Environmental Control System, temperature control

items.question: In the Communications System description, what is the function of the intercom system?
options: To provide internal voice communication between crew members and, where installed, with passengers.
To transmit flight data to air traffic control automatically.
To control hydraulic pressure to the flight controls.
To adjust rotor RPM based on voice commands.
items.explanation: The Communications System section explains that the intercom system allows crew members, and in some configurations passengers, to communicate with each other via headsets and microphones.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - Communications, intercom

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what is the difference in effect between the cyclic (PITCH/ROLL) beep trim switch and the collective (COLL/YAW) beep trim switch?
options: Pressing the cyclic beep trim causes engagement of HOV mode in position-hover, while pressing the collective beep trim causes disengagement of any AFCS collective mode
Both switches have the identical effect of adjusting the currently engaged mode's reference, with no engagement or disengagement function
The cyclic beep trim disengages all AFCS modes, while the collective beep trim engages HOV mode
The collective beep trim only functions on the ground; the cyclic beep trim only functions in flight
items.explanation: The AFCS control panel key describes an asymmetry: pressing the PITCH/ROLL beep trim switch causes engagement of HOV mode in position-hover, while pressing the COLL/YAW beep trim switch causes disengagement of any AFCS collective mode.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key items 23 and 29 (p.7-32/7-33)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, pressing the DCL push-button arms/engages which mode, and what determines which one?
options: Either DCL (Deceleration mode) or NDCL (Autonomous Deceleration mode), depending on the condition
Always DCL mode; NDCL can only be selected from the NAV push-button
Always NDCL mode; DCL is a display-only annunciation with no separate engagement
DCL engages an emergency descent mode unrelated to deceleration approaches
items.explanation: The AFCS control panel key states that pressing the DCL push-button causes one of the following to be armed/engaged according to the condition: DCL - Deceleration mode, or NDCL - Autonomous Deceleration mode.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key item 5 (p.7-30)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, which APP sub-mode is only available for Avionic Phase 6.0 and later?
options: BC (Back course approach mode)
GS (Glide slope approach mode)
VAPP (VOR approach mode)
LOC (Localizer approach mode)
items.explanation: Pressing the APP push-button arms/engages one or more sub-modes depending on the condition: VAPP, LOC, BC, GS, NAPP, NLOC, or NGS. Of these, BC (Back course approach mode) is specifically noted as available only for Avionic Phase 6.0 and later.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key item 7 (p.7-30)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what does pressing the NAV push-button arm or engage?
options: One or more of VOR (VOR navigation mode) or NAV (Autonomous navigation mode), depending on the condition
Only the FMS-coupled NAV mode; VOR navigation is selected from a separate push-button
The WLVL mode as a prerequisite before navigation modes can engage
Only the back course approach mode
items.explanation: The AFCS control panel key states that pressing the NAV push-button causes one or more of the following modes to be armed/engaged, according to the condition: VOR - VOR navigation mode, NAV - Autonomous navigation mode.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key item 11 (p.7-31)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what is required for the TD/H push-button (Transition Down / Transition Down to Hover modes) to be usable?
options: It is only available for Avionic Phase 6.0 and later, and displays "FUNCTION UNAVL" if operated when the option file for TD/TDH/TU modes has not been enabled
It is available on all Avionic Phases with no option-file dependency
It requires both AP1 and AP2 to be disengaged before it can be pressed
It is only usable below 50 KIAS
items.explanation: The AFCS control panel key states the TD/H push-button, only for Avionic Phase 6.0 and later, arms/engages TD (Transition down mode) or TDH (Transition down to hover mode); "FUNCTION UNAVL" is displayed on the PFD if operated when the option file for TD/TDH/TU modes has not been enabled.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key item 15 (p.7-31)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what do the three colored indications on an AFCS mode's active box mean: a green flash, an amber flash that remains solid, and amber chevrons surrounding the box?
options: Green flash = engagement/disengagement transition; amber flash then solid = mode degradation; amber chevrons = excessive deviation from reference for the active mode
Green flash = mode armed; amber flash then solid = mode captured; amber chevrons = mode about to disengage automatically
Green flash = AFCS channel failure; amber flash then solid = normal operation; amber chevrons = pilot override in progress
All three indications mean the same thing: the mode is degraded
items.explanation: The AFCS control panel key describes the collective/pitch/yaw-roll active boxes: they flash green to indicate engagement/disengagement transitions, flash amber and remain solid to indicate mode degradation for the active mode, and are surrounded by amber chevrons to indicate excessive deviation from reference for the active mode.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key items 32, 35, 37 (p.7-33/7-34)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, once the AFCS Collective mode has been automatically uncoupled (UCPL) due to a transition to OEI with power above COEI, what re-couples it?
options: Reducing power to below COEI (Continuous OEI) automatically re-couples the collective mode when the pilot releases the collective
The collective mode re-couples automatically as soon as power drops below COEI, regardless of collective position
Only a manual press of the AP1 or AP2 push-button can re-couple the collective mode after UCPL
UCPL is permanent for the remainder of the flight once it occurs
items.explanation: UCPL indicates the AFCS Collective mode has uncoupled automatically (Avionic Phase 6.0 and later) due to a transition to OEI with power above COEI. Reducing power to below COEI automatically re-couples the collective mode when the pilot releases the collective.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key item 51 (p.7-35)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, how does the SCAS actuator authority compare between the Main Rotor Actuators (MRAs) and the Tail Rotor Actuator (TRA)?
options: The MRA SCAS authority is limited to ±10% of the servoactuator half-stroke, while the TRA SCAS authority is ±20%
Both the MRA and TRA SCAS authority are limited to ±10% of the servoactuator half-stroke
The MRA SCAS authority is ±20% while the TRA SCAS authority is ±10%
SCAS authority is unlimited on both the MRAs and the TRA
items.explanation: The System Description states the MRA SCAS actuator authority is limited to a value corresponding to ±10% of the servoactuator half stroke, while the TRA SCAS actuator has ±20% authority of the servo actuator half-stroke - a safety feature restricting flight control movement in case of a system failure or jam.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Main Rotor Actuators and Tail Rotor Actuator (p.7-36/7-37)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, how does the electromagnetic clutch on the pitch, roll, yaw, and collective trim actuators behave?
options: The actuator shaft is mechanically coupled to the DC motor when the clutch is NOT energized; the shaft is free to rotate when the clutch IS energized
The actuator shaft is mechanically coupled to the DC motor when the clutch IS energized; the shaft is free to rotate when the clutch is NOT energized
The clutch has no effect on shaft coupling; it only controls trim actuator power supply
The clutch permanently locks the shaft regardless of energization state
items.explanation: Each trim actuator (pitch, roll, yaw, collective) is equipped with an electromagnetic clutch providing mechanical coupling between the actuator shaft and the DC motor when the clutch is NOT energized, with the shaft free to rotate if the clutch IS energized - operated by the pilot pressing the relevant trim release control.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Pitch/Roll/Yaw/Collective Trim Actuator (p.7-37/7-38)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what happens on the CAS when the C/Y (yaw) permanent force trim is disengaged?
options: The green C/Y label goes off, and the advisory alert C/Y TRIM OFF plus the caution SAS OFF are generated
The green C/Y label goes off, and only the advisory alert C/Y TRIM OFF is generated, with no caution
The caution ATT OFF is generated, the same as when P/R trim is disengaged
No CAS indication is generated; only the AFCS control panel label changes
items.explanation: The C/Y PTR function on the AFCS page of the EDCU engages the cyclic permanent force trim system; when engaged a green label appears, and when disengaged the green label goes off and the advisory alert C/Y TRIM OFF and the caution SAS OFF are generated on the CAS. (This is distinct from P/R PTR, whose disengagement generates a P/R TRIM OFF advisory and an ATT OFF caution.)
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key item 55 (p.7-35)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, what does an FCS LINK FAIL indication mean?
options: Loss of AFCS mode annunciations and mode datum reference - not necessarily a loss of the underlying AFCS control function itself
Total loss of both AFCS Autopilot channels (AP1 and AP2) with no stabilization remaining
A hydraulic failure in the main rotor actuators requiring immediate landing
Loss of the AFCS control panel's backlighting only
items.explanation: FCS LINK FAIL is defined in the AFCS controls and displays key as loss of AFCS mode annunciations and mode datum reference - a display/annunciation loss, distinct from an actual loss of AFCS stabilization or autopilot function.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key item 53 (p.7-35)

items.question: According to the AFCS System Description, which three push-buttons on the AFCS control panel are inoperative and display "FUNCTION UNAVL" on the PFD if operated?
options: VNAV, WTR, and MOT
IAS, ALT, and HDG
AP1, AP2, and TEST
GA/TU, WLVL, and ATT
items.explanation: The AFCS control panel key states that the VNAV, WTR, and MOT push-buttons are all inoperative on this configuration; "FUNCTION UNAVL" is displayed on the PFD if any of them is operated.
references: AW169 RFM Section 7 - AFCS (Chap 22), Figure 7-12 key items 9, 16, 17 (p.7-30/7-31)
